result.root_cause:
The prompt rules are in place, but small local models (gemma3:4b, qwen3:8b) ignore them. The deterministic safety net, strip_rag_meta, only knows a narrow set of English lead-ins at the start of a line. It misses coordinated nouns, adjectives like "official CvSU", hedge prefixes ("I'm sorry, but based on…"), sentence-internal lead-ins, bold-wrapped lead-ins, lead-ins with a citation in the middle, and every Filipino variant. It also runs only before the guard, so the guard's citation stripping can leave orphaned lead-ins ("According to, X").

Repeats and pushback have no deterministic net at all. Nothing compares the reply with the previous assistant turn or removes blocks repeated inside a reply (the "same 3-bullet fallback twice" symptom). A live-lookup pushback ("just create a list available online") goes back to the LLM with the same grounding, so it naturally regenerates the same fallback. Finally, the VOICE block is longer than it needs to be for the local-CPU prefill budget.

The original transcript failure ("why only trece?" served the static list-of-campuses intent) happened because the cascade classified each message on its own. Step 0.9 now addresses that, but five problems remain:

(a) The detector is too loose. Any short message starting with why, bakit, so, also or "what if", and pushback-shaped closings like "no thanks", bypass the curated tiers.

(b) Follow-up routing has no recency or previous-turn checks, and anchors on the immediately previous user message even when that was itself a follow-up.

(c) A campus named contrastively ("why only trece", "not trece") is treated as the user's campus twice: campus_context makes it sticky for 30 minutes, and `_gather_grounding` derives `wanted` from it. Both re-admit the satellite chunk the user objected to.

(d) The provider-side `[-6:]` slices cap context at 3 turns regardless of `_llm_context`, and untruncated long templates make a bigger window expensive on CPU.

(e) There is no memory of level. `_maybe_state_assumption` only looks at the current message and the app-passed campus.

**A. api/conversation_polish.py: tighten the detector and add helpers**

A1. Split `_FOLLOWUP_OPENER_RE` into two regexes.

`_STRONG_OPENER_RE` is enough on its own when the message is ≤9 words:
```
^\s*(?:what about|how about|and (?:what|how|the|for|if|where|when)|but (?:what|why|how)|then (?:what|how)|is (?:that|it)|does (?:that|it)|are (?:those|they)|why (?:only|just|not)|bakit (?:lang|hindi)|paano naman|pano (?:naman|kung)|ano naman|eh?\s+(?:paano|pano|bakit|yung|ano|sa)|e di|edi|yung (?:sa|para))\b
```
This adds "eh sa" / "e paano" (lone "e") to the Filipino forms.

`_WEAK_OPENER_RE` (`^\s*(?:why|bakit|so|but|also|what if|can i (?:also|still))\b`) counts only if one of these holds:
- the message is ≤4 words; or
- the text AFTER the opener contains a back-reference cue: `_REFERENCE_RE`, or the Filipino/English contrast words `lang|only|just|naman|instead`.

Result: "bakit trece lang?" is True, and "why is tuition free at CvSU?" is False.

A2. Add exclusions, checked first, that make `is_contextual_followup` return False:
